results.name: J1 JBIG2: every corpus JBIG2 image bit-exact vs PDFium (1 declared divergence)
J2 JPX: every corpus JPX image within ±2 of PDFium (1 declared divergence: SMaskInData 1 pre-composited by PDFium)
J3 JPX vs OpenJPEG: 40 generated codestreams — lossless = source exactly, lossy ±1
J4 PDF wiring: /Indexed JPX keeps raw indices (issue12213 exact), /SMaskInData yields a soft mask, JPX size wins over /Width
N1 JPX garbage / empty / random bytes throw a clean error, quickly
N2 JPX hand-built minimal codestream decodes (empty packet → mid-grey), and every truncation of it is bounded
N3 JPX oversize SIZ (2^31 × 2^31), zero tile size, 32 levels on 8×8 and 70 000 tiles are refused or bounded
N4 JPX truncated real codestreams (every 7th cut of a generated lossy RGB stream) keep the decoded part, never hang
N5 JBIG2 garbage, empty and truncated segment streams are bounded and never throw out of the decoder
N6 JBIG2 bomb (bomb_giant.pdf: a page claiming a huge region) is refused fast with bounded memory
N7 a PDF whose JPX stream is garbage renders the rest of the page (image becomes the disclosed placeholder, no throw)
